NP Presspad 1.2.0 — Custom fields that actually sync

**This release needs a companion plugin update.** Update it on each of your sites — WordPress will offer it under Plugins, and the app will remind you if a site is still on the old version. Until you do, custom fields on that site behave as before.

## What's new for you

- **Custom fields registered in code now sync.** If your field groups are defined by your theme or a plugin rather than in the ACF admin screens, the app could show the fields but never their contents — an empty repeater on a post that plainly had data. It also couldn't save into them: edits looked like they worked and quietly went nowhere. Both directions now work.
- **The shortcode button works.** It was asking your site for a list of shortcodes through an address that never existed, so it always reported "No shortcodes found". Your site's shortcodes now appear.
- **Your existing posts catch up on their own.** The first sync after updating re-reads custom field values for posts you haven't edited locally, so the fields fill in without you touching anything. Posts with unsaved changes or an unresolved conflict are left alone.

## Also fixed

- **Custom field values are no longer cleared when a sync can't see them.** If a response didn't mention custom fields — an old plugin, or a site where you lack editing rights on a post — the app treated that silence as "these fields are now empty" and wiped its copy. It now keeps what it has.
- **Repeater rows refresh after a sync.** Rows shown on screen were only ever built when the panel opened, so values arriving from a sync or a conflict resolution didn't appear until you navigated away and back.

## For site owners

Values are readable only by someone who could already edit that post in wp-admin — they are not made public. If you would rather the plugin didn't expose them at all, add `add_filter( 'wpoe_expose_acf_values', '__return_false' );` to your site.

The plugin's status endpoint no longer reveals its version number to anonymous visitors.
